operator_io_quirks: Table/column names are all lowercase here, but DDL uses quoted "reviews"/"categories" and a quoted constraint name "PRIMARY" — identifier quoting must survive.
reviews has 1,964,856 rows and podcasts 108,578 — read_schema must rowid-sample (max_rows_per_table) and still get full count(*) for original_sizes.
runs has no PK and no FK; it is a tiny 12-row log table — TS will still generate ~30-2500 rows for it.
reviews has no PK at all (pk=[]), so sample_fresh_primary_keys is a no-op there; only unique-column dedup applies (none declared).
categories has composite PK (podcast_id, category) — composite-PK member gets max_l0=30 cap in TS.
FK reviews.podcast_id -> podcasts with parent_col NULL (same-name resolution) and parent_exists true; categories.podcast_id likewise.
reviews.podcast_id has only 8,587 distinct values over 1.9M rows — heavy many-to-one; TS draws child FK values with replacement from parent's final column, so duplicates are expected and fine.
categories.podcast_id distinct 103,230 < podcasts 108,578 — some podcasts have no category; FK is not surjective.

created_at is TEXT storing ISO-8601 with timezone offset '2018-04-24T12:05:16-07:00' — declared TEXT so TS dispatches to String, NOT Date; the 'T' and '-07:00' will not be reproduced by the String fuzzer.
run_at is TEXT storing 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' — also String fuzzer, not Date; format not preserved.
podcast_id / author_id are 32-hex and 15-hex uppercase strings — String fuzzer over a-zA-Z0-9() will not match the hex shape.
rating is INTEGER with only 5 distinct values (1..5) — Number fuzzer will produce values far outside [1,5].
operator_ts_expectations: podcasts.podcast_id (TEXT PK, single-column) -> String fuzzer, max_l0=inf, fresh random strings over a-zA-Z0-9() length ~[0,20]; original 32-hex shape lost.
reviews.podcast_id / categories.podcast_id -> FK fill from podcasts' final podcast_id column with replacement; many duplicates, some podcasts unreferenced.
categories composite PK (podcast_id, category) -> both String fuzzers with max_l0=30; PK dedup keeps first occurrence, so category cardinality collapses.
rating INTEGER -> Number fuzzer scale 0, range [-1,1] perturbed by +-1/+-2; almost all values outside the real 1..5 -> implausible ratings (likely FN driver for rating predicates).

itunes_id, max_rowid, reviews_added INTEGER -> Number fuzzer; max_rowid ~3.3M and reviews_added ~1.2M originals are far above the [-1,1] fresh range, so only the 5 sampled originals (perturbed) reach that magnitude.
created_at / run_at TEXT -> String fuzzer; no date template, so date-range predicates on these columns will mostly miss (FN) and equality on exact timestamps will rarely hit (FN).
title/content/slug/itunes_url TEXT -> String fuzzer with contaminate (prefix/suffix/drop) — LIKE '%...%' predicates may accidentally match (FP) but exact equality rarely.
runs has no PK/unique -> no dedup; TS will emit ~30-2500 rows of random strings/numbers into a 12-row log table.
reviews has no PK and no unique columns -> no dedup at all; 1.9M-row table gets a random size (30..2500 or level-based), so joins to podcasts are sparse.
String fuzzer adds str(i+1)/str(i-1) for int-like elements and strips '%' — irrelevant here since no int-like strings in text columns.
No Date/Time/Bool/Bit fuzzers fire on this DB (all TEXT/INTEGER) — TS never produces the ISO timestamp shape.
FK child draws from parent's FINAL filtered column: podcasts PK dedup is a no-op (already unique), so FK values are valid podcast_ids.
